top.en: At [~0:Worlds] 2022, this guy got played like a toilet bowl by every Worlds ADC. [~1:Redmi] called him out by name, saying that as the first seed, making the quarterfinals was enough and he lacked any fighting spirit. In the semifinals, [~2:Gumayusi] handed him the biggest ADC skill gap in history, and Gumayusi mocked him to his face, saying 'now you know why JDG didn't want to play against our bot lane.' Aphelios and Lulu got completely plowed by Lucian and Nami for three games, and even in the fourth game with Jinx and Karma begging him not to collapse in the laning phase, he still got brutally solo-killed in lane. In his prime, [~3:369]'s Sejuani came down to help him, but he turned around and handed over a free kill while still getting solo-killed by Gumayusi. You wasted the peak of JDG's top, jungle, and mid that year; if JDG had any other ADC that year, they would have been title contenders. I hate you so much, I really hate you. The second opportunity was given to you last year in the fifth game against T1, where you played Jinx and [~4:nuo]ed to the absolute limit. Change you for any other ADC who has even a shred of courage, and they would have beaten T1. Why does [~5:Jiaqi] have everyone loving him so much? And all you have is [~0:hope]? Because ever since 2022, the LPL has suffered for a strong ADC for far too long. Why can [~2:Gumayusi] play so wild at Worlds and T1 win three straight titles? The biggest problem is that our region has no young ADCs who can fight in lane. A level like [~0:hope] being the first seed every year is just a tragedy. The designated Korean forum synonym for trash is literally Hope, how embarrassing—whoever they call trash, they just say he's Hope. Can you please retire? I'm genuinely begging you 🙏 please retire, I'm begging you to retire !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I'm begging you!! Retire! Your retirement would be the greatest contribution to the LPL! The third chance was given to you, and as the first seed you go 0-3 without winning a single game, straight home in the round of 16. Do not let me see you in the LPL next season, and if any team takes you, I will hate them for life.

notes.context: Fan nickname for the player Hope, playing on his name's meaning.

thread.en: From S1 to S15 (the old group stage format), no LPL or LCK team was ever eliminated from the main event without winning a single game. Gen.G in S8 was the LCK's all-time low: 1-5, but they at least took one Bo1 win. LPL's worst years, like LGD in S5, EDG in S7, or FPX in S11, all had wins. It wasn't until S16 today with AL that we saw the first team from the Chinese or Korean regions to go 0-0 in series and 0-all in games. If we expand the scope beyond Worlds to include MSI, the Esports World Cup, and the Saudi Cup, AL is still the first team to go home without a single win. [破防]

The early game was basically just constantly wiping the bot lane's ass. Besides, Akali has a shroud so you can't catch her, and Kled in the top lane wasn't easy to gank either. I feel like Nocturne flying in all by himself was super fragile, and Annie couldn't follow up (though I feel like following up would've been useless anyway), Tahm Kench had to protect that VIP in the bot lane, and Olaf was practically invisible. Long story short, when TES picks Nocturne, you always have [~1:Oil God]'s Orianna carrying a ball, and you always have 369's Ambessa [~2:carrying it straight in]. If this Nocturne flies in and realizes he's completely by himself, what's he supposed to do? Is he seriously expected to single-handedly assassinate a gigafed Xayah with an ultimate? Or kill an Akali with a shroud? He definitely deserves blame for the 16th-place finish, but given Tarzan's form and league performance this year, take a look at what the other guys in the laning phase were doing besides Shanks?

thread.en: Facts have proven that the double-elimination format is just garbage. A team gets 3-0'd, gets a second life, wins all the way to the finals, and then has to face a hot team that's been waiting for half a month with zero momentum, and if the winner loses they just lose with no second life. Isn't that obviously unreasonable? If you're gonna do double-elimination then commit to it and make a strict rule that every team gets two lives and it's not over until they're used up, or else ditch this garbage double-elimination and switch back to single-elimination so it's actually exciting to watch.

top.problem: Meaning reversed. 'Expecting AL is worse than expecting TES' implies TES is the better expectation, but the translation says 'Expecting AL... is worse than expecting TES', which is ambiguous or implies the opposite comparison structure depending on interpretation, but more critically, the Chinese 'A不如B' means 'A is not as good as B' or 'B is better than A'. The translation 'Expecting AL... is worse than expecting TES' is actually a correct literal translation of the structure, BUT in context of fan comments, '不如' often means 'is not as good as'. Let's re-read: '世界赛期待al不如期待滔搏' -> 'Expecting AL at Worlds is not as good as expecting TES'. The translation says 'Expecting AL... is worse than expecting TES'. This is semantically equivalent. Wait, is it? 'Worse than' is a valid translation of '不如' in this context. Let's look closer. Actually, the translation is acceptable. Let's check other items first. Re-evaluating: '不如' means 'not as good as'. 'Expecting AL is not as good as expecting TES'. The translation 'Expecting AL... is worse than expecting TES' is fine. I will mark it OK.
